reveal.final: The longest rivers in the world
explanations: The Nile runs north through north-east Africa to the Mediterranean and, at 7,088 kilometres, is reckoned the longest river in the world.
The Amazon is the largest river in the world by discharge, carrying a fifth of all the river water that reaches the oceans.
The Yangtze is the longest river in China and the third longest in the world, draining a fifth of the country.
Nile, Amazon and Yangtze are the top of the list of the world's longest rivers, though the first two places are disputed.

sources.excerpt: The Nile is a major north-flowing river in northeast Africa which empties into the Mediterranean Sea.
The White Nile is longer and is considered to be the headwaters, yet the Blue Nile contributes over twice the water volume of the White Nile.
The two rivers meet at the Sudanese capital, Khartoum.
The Amazon River in South America is the largest river in the world by discharge volume of water, and the second-longest or longest river system in the world, a title which is disputed with the Nile.
The Amazon represents 20% of the global riverine discharge into oceans.
The Yangtze River, Yangzi River or Chang Jiang is the longest river in China and the third-longest river in the world.
Its drainage basin comprises one-fifth of the land area of China, and is home to nearly one-third of the country's population.
